23.text: Now David was old and full of days; and he made Solomon his son king over Israel.
He gathered together all the princes of Israel, with the priests and the Levites.
The Levites were counted from thirty years old and upward; and their number by their polls, man by man, was thirty-eight thousand.
David said, “Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of the LORD’s house, six thousand were officers and judges,
four thousand were doorkeepers, and four thousand praised the LORD with the instruments which I made for giving praise.”
David divided them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel, three.
The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers’ households of Ladan.
The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.
Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah didn’t have many sons; therefore they became a fathers’ house in one reckoning.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.

The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses; and Aaron was separated that he should sanctify the most holy things, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to him, and to bless in his name forever.
But as for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
The son of Eliezer was Rehabiah the chief; and Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
The son of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died, and had no sons, but daughters only; and their relatives, the sons of Kish, took them as wives.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three.

These were the sons of Levi after their fathers’ houses, even the heads of the fathers’ houses of those who were counted individually, in the number of names by their polls, who did the work for the service of the LORD’s house, from twenty years old and upward.
For David said, “The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people; and he dwells in Jerusalem forever.
Also the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all its vessels for its service.”
For by the last words of David the sons of Levi were counted, from twenty years old and upward.
For their duty was to wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of the LORD’s house—in the courts, in the rooms, and in the purifying of all holy things, even the work of the service of God’s house;

for the show bread also, and for the fine flour for a meal offering, whether of unleavened wafers, or of that which is baked in the pan, or of that which is soaked, and for all measurements of quantity and size;
and to stand every morning to thank and praise the LORD, and likewise in the evening;
and to offer all burnt offerings to the LORD on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts, in number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually before the LORD;
and that they should keep the duty of the Tent of Meeting, the duty of the holy place, and the duty of the sons of Aaron their brothers for the service of the LORD’s house.

24.text: These were the divisions of the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and had no children; therefore Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
David, with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, divided them according to their ordering in their service.

There were more chief men found of the sons of Eleazar than of the sons of Ithamar; and they were divided like this: of the sons of Eleazar there were sixteen, heads of fathers’ houses; and of the sons of Ithamar, according to their fathers’ houses, eight.
Thus they were divided impartially by drawing lots; for there were princes of the sanctuary and princes of God, both of the sons of Eleazar, and of the sons of Ithamar.

Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe, who was of the Levites, wrote them in the presence of the king, the princes, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites; one fathers’ house being taken for Eleazar, and one taken for Ithamar.
Now the first lot came out to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
the twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
This was their ordering in their service, to come into the LORD’s house according to the ordinance given to them by Aaron their father, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
Of the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
Of the Izharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
The brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The son of Jaaziah: Beno.
The sons of Merari by Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
Of Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
Of Kish, the son of Kish: Jerahmeel.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites after their fathers’ houses.

These likewise cast lots even as their brothers the sons of Aaron in the presence of David the king, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites, the fathers’ households of the chief even as those of his younger brother.

25.text: Moreover, David and the captains of the army set apart for the service certain of the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who were to prophesy with harps, with stringed instruments, and with cymbals. The number of those who did the work according to their service was:
of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah. The sons of Asaph were under the hand of Asaph, who prophesied at the order of the king.

Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the hands of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied in giving thanks and praising the LORD with the harp.
Of Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All these were the sons of Heman the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn. God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

All these were under the hands of their father for song in the LORD’s house, with cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps, for the service of God’s house: Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman being under the order of the king.
The number of them, with their brothers who were instructed in singing to the LORD, even all who were skillful, was two hundred eighty-eight.
They cast lots for their offices, all alike, the small as well as the great, the teacher as well as the student.
Now the first lot came out for Asaph to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, he and his brothers and sons were twelve;
the third to Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the fourth to Izri, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the seventh to Jesharelah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the thirteenth, Shubael, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the fourteenth, Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
for the twenty-fourth to Romamti-Ezer, his sons and his brothers, twelve.

26.text: For the divisions of the doorkeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.
Obed-Edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth; for God blessed him.
Sons were also born to Shemaiah his son, who ruled over the house of their father; for they were mighty men of valor.
The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, whose relatives were valiant men, Elihu, and Semachiah.
All these were of the sons of Obed-Edom with their sons and their brothers, able men in strength for the service: sixty-two of Obed-Edom.
Meshelemiah had sons and brothers, eighteen valiant men.
Also Hosah, of the children of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (for though he was not the firstborn, yet his father made him chief),
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
Of these were the divisions of the doorkeepers, even of the chief men, having offices like their brothers, to minister in the LORD’s house.
They cast lots, the small as well as the great, according to their fathers’ houses, for every gate.
The lot eastward fell to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a wise counselor, they cast lots; and his lot came out northward.
To Obed-Edom southward; and to his sons the storehouse.
To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway that goes up, watchman opposite watchman.
Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the storehouse two and two.
For Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar.
These were the divisions of the doorkeepers; of the sons of the Korahites, and of the sons of Merari.
Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God’s house and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ households belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of the LORD’s house.
Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites:
Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasuries.
His brothers: of Eliezer, Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.

This Shelomoth and his brothers were over all the treasuries of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ households, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the army, had dedicated.
They dedicated some of the plunder won in battles to repair the LORD’s house.

All that Samuel the seer, Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah had dedicated, whoever had dedicated anything, it was under the hand of Shelomoth and of his brothers.
Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.

Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred men of valor, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of the LORD and for the service of the king.

Of the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief of the Hebronites, according to their generations by fathers’ households. They were sought for in the fortieth year of the reign of David, and mighty men of valor were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.

His relatives, men of valor, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers’ households, whom King David made overseers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.

27.text: Now the children of Israel after their number, the heads of fathers’ households and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in any matter of the divisions which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year—of every division were twenty-four thousand.
Over the first division for the first month was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
He was of the children of Perez, the chief of all the captains of the army for the first month.
Over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite and his division, and Mikloth the ruler; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The third captain of the army for the third month was Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the chief priest. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
This is that Benaiah who was the mighty man of the thirty and over the thirty. Of his division was Ammizabad his son.
The fourth captain for the fourth month was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
The fifth captain for the fifth month was Shamhuth the Izrahite. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
The sixth captain for the sixth month was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
The seventh captain for the seventh month was Helez the Pelonite, of the children of Ephraim. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eighth captain for the eighth month was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
The ninth captain for the ninth month was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjamites. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
The tenth captain for the tenth month was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eleventh captain for the eleventh month was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephraim. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
The twelfth captain for the twelfth month was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
Furthermore over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites, Eliezer the son of Zichri was the ruler; of the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
of Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; of Aaron, Zadok;
of Judah, Elihu, one of the brothers of David; of Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;
of Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; of Naphtali, Jeremoth the son of Azriel;
of the children of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;
of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; of Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;
of Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the captains of the tribes of Israel.
But David didn’t take the number of them from twenty years old and under, because the LORD had said he would increase Israel like the stars of the sky.
Joab the son of Zeruiah began to take a census, but didn’t finish; and wrath came on Israel for this. The number wasn’t put into the account in the chronicles of King David.
Over the king’s treasures was Azmaveth the son of Adiel. Over the treasures in the fields, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers was Jonathan the son of Uzziah;
Over those who did the work of the field for tillage of the ground was Ezri the son of Chelub.
Over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite. Over the increase of the vineyards for the wine cellars was Zabdi the Shiphmite.
Over the olive trees and the sycamore trees that were in the lowland was Baal Hanan the Gederite. Over the cellars of oil was Joash.
Over the herds that fed in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite. Over the herds that were in the valleys was Shaphat the son of Adlai.
Over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite. Over the donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite. Over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite.
All these were the rulers of the property which was King David’s.
Also Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe. Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.
Ahithophel was the king’s counselor. Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.
After Ahithophel was Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. Joab was the captain of the king’s army.

28.text: David assembled all the princes of Israel, the princes of the tribes, the captains of the companies who served the king by division, the captains of thousands, the captains of hundreds, and the rulers over all the substance and possessions of the king and of his sons, with the officers and the mighty men, even all the mighty men of valor, to Jerusalem.

Then David the king stood up on his feet and said, “Hear me, my brothers and my people! As for me, it was in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the LORD’s covenant, and for the footstool of our God; and I had prepared for the building.
But God said to me, ‘You shall not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.’

However the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me out of all the house of my father to be king over Israel forever. For he has chosen Judah to be prince; and in the house of Judah, the house of my father; and among the sons of my father he took pleasure in me to make me king over all Israel.
Of all my sons (for the LORD has given me many sons), he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the LORD’s kingdom over Israel.
He said to me, ‘Solomon, your son, shall build my house and my courts; for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
I will establish his kingdom forever if he continues to do my commandments and my ordinances, as it is today.’

Now therefore, in the sight of all Israel, the LORD’s assembly, and in the audience of our God, observe and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, that you may possess this good land, and leave it for an inheritance to your children after you forever.

You, Solomon my son, know the God of your father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind; for the LORD searches all hearts, and understands all the imaginations of the thoughts. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever.
Take heed now, for the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong, and do it.”
Then David gave to Solomon his son the plans for the porch of the temple, for its houses, for its treasuries, for its upper rooms, for its inner rooms, for the place of the mercy seat;
and the plans of all that he had by the Spirit, for the courts of the LORD’s house, for all the surrounding rooms, for the treasuries of God’s house, and for the treasuries of the dedicated things;
also for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the work of the service of the LORD’s house, and for all the vessels of service in the LORD’s house—
of gold by weight for the gold for all vessels of every kind of service, for all the vessels of silver by weight, for all vessels of every kind of service;

by weight also for the lamp stands of gold, and for its lamps, of gold, by weight for every lamp stand and for its lamps; and for the lamp stands of silver, by weight for every lamp stand and for its lamps, according to the use of every lamp stand;
and the gold by weight for the tables of show bread, for every table; and silver for the tables of silver;
and the forks, the basins, and the cups, of pure gold; and for the golden bowls by weight for every bowl; and for the silver bowls by weight for every bowl;
and for the altar of incense, refined gold by weight; and gold for the plans for the chariot, and the cherubim that spread out and cover the ark of the LORD’s covenant.
“All this”, David said, “I have been made to understand in writing from the LORD’s hand, even all the works of this pattern.”

David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed, for the LORD God, even my God, is with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of the LORD’s house is finished.

Behold, there are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of God’s house. Every willing man who has skill for any kind of service shall be with you in all kinds of work. Also the captains and all the people will be entirely at your command.”

29.text: David the king said to all the assembly, “Solomon my son, whom alone God has chosen, is yet young and tender, and the work is great; for the palace is not for man, but for the LORD God.

Now I have prepared with all my might for the house of my God the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, the bronze for the things of bronze, iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood, also onyx stones, stones to be set, stones for inlaid work of various colors, all kinds of precious stones, and marble stones in abundance.

In addition, because I have set my affection on the house of my God, since I have a treasure of my own of gold and silver, I give it to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house:
even three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, with which to overlay the walls of the houses;

of gold for the things of gold, and of silver for the things of silver, and for all kinds of work to be made by the hands of artisans. Who then offers willingly to consecrate himself today to the LORD?”
Then the princes of the fathers’ households, and the princes of the tribes of Israel, and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, with the rulers over the king’s work, offered willingly;

and they gave for the service of God’s house of gold five thousand talents and ten thousand darics, of silver ten thousand talents, of bronze eighteen thousand talents, and of iron one hundred thousand talents.
People with whom precious stones were found gave them to the treasure of the LORD’s house, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
Then the people rejoiced, because they offered willingly, because with a perfect heart they offered willingly to the LORD; and David the king also rejoiced with great joy.
Therefore David blessed the LORD before all the assembly; and David said, “You are blessed, LORD, the God of Israel our father, forever and ever.

Yours, LORD, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty! For all that is in the heavens and on the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, LORD, and you are exalted as head above all.
Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all! In your hand is power and might! It is in your hand to make great, and to give strength to all!
Now therefore, our God, we thank you and praise your glorious name.
But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and we have given you of your own.
For we are strangers before you and foreigners, as all our fathers were. Our days on the earth are as a shadow, and there is no remaining.
LORD our God, all this store that we have prepared to build you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and is all your own.

I know also, my God, that you try the heart and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things. Now I have seen with joy your people, who are present here, offer willingly to you.
LORD, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, our fathers, keep this desire forever in the thoughts of the heart of your people, and prepare their heart for you;
and give to Solomon my son a perfect heart, to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, and to do all these things, and to build the palace, for which I have made provision.”

Then David said to all the assembly, “Now bless the LORD your God!” All the assembly blessed the LORD, the God of their fathers, and bowed down their heads and prostrated themselves before the LORD and the king.

They sacrificed sacrifices to the LORD and offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the next day after that day, even one thousand bulls, one thousand rams, and one thousand lambs, with their drink offerings and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel,
and ate and drank before the LORD on that day with great gladness. They made Solomon the son of David king the second time, and anointed him before the LORD to be prince, and Zadok to be priest.
Then Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king instead of David his father, and prospered; and all Israel obeyed him.
All the princes, the mighty men, and also all of the sons of King David submitted themselves to Solomon the king.
The LORD magnified Solomon exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and gave to him such royal majesty as had not been on any king before him in Israel.
Now David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
The time that he reigned over Israel was forty years; he reigned seven years in Hebron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
Now the acts of David the king, first and last, behold, they are written in the history of Samuel the seer, and in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the history of Gad the seer,
with all his reign and his might, and the events that involved him, Israel, and all the kingdoms of the lands.

chapters.title: From Adam to Israel and Edom
chapters.summary: The book opens with a list of names and no story. It runs from Adam through Noah to Noah’s three sons. It names the peoples that came from Japheth, Ham, and Shem. Shem’s line leads to Abraham. Abraham’s sons are Isaac and Ishmael, with more sons by Keturah. Isaac’s sons are Esau and Israel. The rest of the chapter lists Esau’s family and the kings and chiefs of Edom.
chapters.meaning: Verse 1 is three names with no verb. The list assumes readers know the stories from Genesis. It starts with all humanity before it narrows. Verses 5–23 name many nations, and only then comes Abraham (verse 27). Verse 34 uses the name Israel, not Jacob. Edom, Israel’s neighbor and rival, receives twenty verses (verses 35–54). The book sets one people’s history inside the history of everyone.

chapters.title: Judah’s families and David’s ancestors
chapters.summary: The chapter lists the twelve sons of Israel and then follows Judah. Judah’s first sons were born to a Canaanite woman. Tamar, his daughter-in-law, bore him Perez and Zerah. The line of Perez runs through Boaz and Jesse to David, the seventh son. David’s sisters and their warrior sons are named. Long lists follow for Caleb’s and Jerahmeel’s families. One man with no sons gives his daughter to his Egyptian servant. The chapter ends with families of scribes who were Kenites.
chapters.meaning: Verse 55 ends Judah’s record with a trade and a foreign origin. These families were scribes, and they were Kenites. Judges 1:16 says the Kenites came from Moses’s in-laws. The chapter has already named a Canaanite mother (verse 3). It names Tamar (verse 4) and an Ishmaelite father (verse 17). It records an Egyptian servant who married into the line (verses 34–35). The list of David’s own tribe makes no effort to hide outsiders.

chapters.title: David’s children and the royal line after exile
chapters.summary: The chapter lists David’s sons born in Hebron and in Jerusalem. It names his daughter Tamar. Then it lists the kings of Judah from Solomon to Josiah’s sons. Jeconiah, also called Jehoiachin, is named “the captive.” His sons include Shealtiel and Pedaiah. Zerubbabel appears in the next generation. The list continues for several generations after the exile.
chapters.meaning: Verse 17 gives a king a new title: “the captive.” The list does not stop with him. Verses 17–24 carry David’s family on for generations with no throne. Zerubbabel in verse 19 later leads the return (Ezra 3:2). None of these men is called king. Yet each name is kept in order. Second Samuel 7:16 promised David a lasting house, and the list shows it surviving.

chapters.title: Judah, Jabez, craftspeople, and Simeon’s settlements
chapters.summary: The chapter adds more clans of Judah. A man named Jabez prays for blessing, more land, and protection from harm. God grants his request. The list names a valley of craftsmen, a guild of linen workers, and royal potters. Then it turns to Simeon’s towns in the south. Some Simeonites move to find pasture for their flocks. In Hezekiah’s time they take land at Gedor. Others defeat a remnant of Amalek at Mount Seir.
chapters.meaning: This family list keeps a record of trades. Verse 14 names a valley of craftsmen. Verse 21 names families that worked fine linen. Verse 23 names potters who lived “with the king for his work.” So some families served in royal workshops. The list treats that work as worth remembering beside warriors and chiefs. A reader after the exile could trace a craft as well as a bloodline.

chapters.title: Eastern tribes, prayer, and captivity
chapters.summary: Reuben was Israel’s firstborn, but he lost the birthright by wronging his father. It passed to Joseph’s sons, while Judah produced the ruler. The chapter lists Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan. In a war with the Hagrites they cry to God, and he helps them. They take many animals and captives. The verses show that standing in this family did not rest on birth alone.

chapters.title: Saul dies at Gilboa
chapters.summary: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa. Saul’s three sons are killed, and archers wound him. He falls on his own sword. The Philistines strip him and put his head in the temple of Dagon. Men of Jabesh Gilead take the bodies and bury them. The writer says Saul died for his unfaithfulness. He did not keep the LORD’s word, and he consulted a medium. So the LORD gave the kingdom to David.
chapters.meaning: Chronicles reduces Saul’s whole reign to the day of his death. Verses 13–14 then add a verdict not found in this form in Samuel. They name three failures. He broke the LORD’s word, asked a medium, and did not ask the LORD. First Samuel 28:6 says Saul asked and received no answer. The two books describe the same end in different words. Seeking the LORD becomes a test for every later king in this book.

chapters.summary: David consults his commanders and the whole assembly about the ark. All agree to bring it from Kiriath Jearim. They carry it on a new cart with music and singing. At a threshing floor the oxen stumble. Uzza puts out his hand to steady the ark, and God strikes him dead. David is angry and then afraid. He leaves the ark at the house of Obed-Edom. chapters.meaning: The plan began with wide agreement. Verse 4 says it seemed right to all the people. Agreement did not make the method right. chapters.summary: The ark is set in its tent, and David offers sacrifices. He gives every person bread, meat, and raisins. He appoints Levites to thank and praise the LORD before the ark. The altar and the daily sacrifices stay there with Zadok. Worship remains divided between song and sacrifice until the temple is built.

He tells Solomon that he wanted to build the house himself. The LORD refused because David had shed much blood. A son named Solomon, a man of rest, would build it. chapters.title: Levitical service is organized
chapters.summary: David is old and makes Solomon king. He counts the Levites aged thirty and above. There are thirty-eight thousand. Most will oversee the work of the LORD’s house. Others will be officers, judges, gatekeepers, and musicians. The families of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari are listed. The Levites will no longer carry the tabernacle. They will help the priests with courts, rooms, bread, flour, measures, and daily praise.
chapters.meaning: Numbers 4 gave the Levites the work of carrying the tabernacle. Verse 25 says the LORD has given his people rest in Jerusalem. Verse 26 draws the result: nothing needs to be carried now. The Levites receive new duties suited to a fixed house (verses 28–32). These include cleaning, baking, and checking weights and sizes. They also stand to thank and praise each morning and evening. Verse 14 notes that Moses’s own sons served as ordinary Levites.

chapters.title: Priestly divisions are assigned by lot
chapters.summary: David organizes the priests, the sons of Aaron. Eleazar’s family has sixteen heads, and Ithamar’s has eight. They are divided by lot, since both families have leaders. A Levite scribe records the result before the king and the priests. Twenty-four divisions are named in order. The eighth lot falls to Abijah. The remaining Levites also cast lots for their duties. The chief’s household and the youngest brother’s are treated alike.
chapters.meaning: The priests’ turns of service are fixed by lot. Verse 5 gives the reason: both branches had officers of rank. A lot keeps either side from favoring its own. Verse 6 says a scribe wrote the results down before witnesses. Verse 31 extends the method to the other Levites. A leading household gets no better place than a younger brother’s. Luke 1:5 later names a priest from the division of Abijah (verse 10).

chapters.title: Musicians, prophecy, and shared assignments
chapters.summary: David and his commanders set apart musicians for the temple. They come from the families of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun. They are to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals. Heman has fourteen sons and three daughters. All serve under their fathers’ direction. There are two hundred eighty-eight trained singers. They cast lots for their duties. Twenty-four groups of twelve are listed in order.
chapters.meaning: Verses 1–3 call the musicians’ work prophesying. The text treats temple song as speech from God as well as to him. Verse 7 says all two hundred eighty-eight were trained and skilled. Verse 8 then describes how duties were given out. The lot fell on small and great alike. Teacher and student stood in the same draw. Training belongs to the service, and rank earns no advantage.

chapters.title: Gatekeepers, stored gifts, and public duties
chapters.summary: The chapter lists the gatekeepers by family. Obed-Edom has sixty-two able descendants, for God blessed him. One father makes a younger son chief. Lots decide which family guards each gate. Guards are posted daily on every side. Other Levites keep the treasuries and the dedicated gifts. These gifts include spoil given by Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab. Still others serve as officers and judges across Israel.
chapters.meaning: Verse 20 puts a named man over the treasures. The verses after it name more keepers and their families (verses 21–26). A named duty means someone answers for what is stored. Verses 27–28 list where the dedicated things came from. Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab all gave spoil. These men were rivals in life, and their gifts are kept together. Verse 24 places a descendant of Moses over the treasuries.

chapters.title: Army rotations and royal property
chapters.summary: The chapter lists the army’s twelve divisions. Each has twenty-four thousand men and serves one month a year. A leader is named for each tribe. David did not count those under twenty, since God promised many descendants. Stewards manage the king’s storehouses, fields, vineyards, and olive trees. Others manage herds, camels, donkeys, and flocks. Two of these stewards are foreigners. The king’s counselors are named last.
chapters.meaning: Verse 1 describes service “month by month.” Each division serves one month and goes home for eleven. The burden is shared in turns across the year. Verses 25–31 list the men who managed crops, wine, oil, and animals. An Ishmaelite keeps the camels, and a Hagrite keeps the flocks (verses 30–31). The kingdom depends on storekeepers and herdsmen as well as soldiers. Verses 23–24 recall the census that brought wrath.

chapters.title: David gives Solomon plans and a charge
chapters.summary: David gathers Israel’s leaders in Jerusalem and stands to speak. He wanted to build a house for the ark. God refused him as a man of war and chose Solomon. David charges Solomon to know God and serve him with a whole heart. He gives him the plans for every room and court. He gives the weights of gold and silver for each lampstand, table, and bowl. He says all of it came in writing from the LORD’s hand. He tells Solomon to be strong and do the work.
chapters.meaning: Solomon receives complete plans in verses 11–19. Verse 20 shows that plans do not finish a building. He must still “be strong and courageous, and do it.” Moses spoke nearly the same words to Joshua (Deuteronomy 31:7–8). The promise in the verse has a term: until the work is finished. Verse 9 states the condition that covers his whole life. Seeking God brings finding him, and leaving him brings rejection.

chapters.title: Gifts, prayer, a new king, and David's death
chapters.summary: David tells the assembly what he has given for the temple from his own treasure. The leaders give gold, silver, bronze, iron, and precious stones. The people rejoice because the gifts are given freely. David blesses the LORD before them all. He says everything in heaven and earth belongs to God. He asks God to keep the people’s hearts loyal and to help Solomon. Solomon is made king, and Zadok priest. David dies at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor.
chapters.meaning: Verses 2–8 list gifts on a huge scale. In verse 14 David refuses to take credit for them. Everything comes from God, and the givers return what was his. Verse 15 calls Israel strangers and temporary residents, as their fathers were. The king says this while holding land, city, and throne. Verse 9 traces the people’s joy to giving willingly. Verse 17 says God tests the heart and is pleased with honesty.

people.role: Ancestor remembered in family lists and praise
people.relations: Husband of Sarah. Father of Ishmael and Isaac. Uncle of Lot.

people.role: Abraham’s son with a named descendant list

people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Isaac
people.role: Abraham’s son, named in the list and in praise
people.relations: Husband of Rebekah. Father of Esau and Jacob.
people.meaning: He is Abraham’s son, and his sons are Esau and Israel. David’s song recalls God’s oath to Isaac. David’s last prayer names him with Abraham and Israel.

people.name: Esau
people.role: Ancestor of Edom
people.relations: Twin brother of Jacob. Ancestor of Edom.

people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jacob
people.role: Israel’s ancestor recalled in families and praise
people.relations: Son of Isaac and Rebekah. Father of twelve sons and Dinah.

people.relations: Son of Jacob and Leah. Father of Perez and Zerah through Tamar.

people.name: Tamar
people.role: Mother of Perez and Zerah in Judah’s line
people.relations: Widow of Er and Onan. Mother of Perez and Zerah.

people.role: Ancestor between Boaz and Jesse

people.meaning: He is the son of Boaz and the father of Jesse. The list tells no story about him.

people.relations: Son of Obed. Father of seven sons and of Zeruiah and Abigail.

people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Josiah
people.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.relations: Son of Amon and Jedidah. Father of Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Shallum.
people.meaning: He is Amon’s son. The list names his four sons: Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Shallum. From here the list follows Jehoiakim’s family.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoiakim
people.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.relations: Son of Josiah and Zebidah. Earlier name Eliakim. Father of Jehoiachin.
people.meaning: He is Josiah’s second son. The list names Jeconiah and Zedekiah under him. It follows Jeconiah’s sons next.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoiachin
people.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.relations: Son of Jehoiakim and Nehushta. Nephew of Zedekiah.
people.meaning: The list calls him Jeconiah, the captive. It names his sons, starting with Shealtiel. The family line runs on through Pedaiah and Zerubbabel.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zedekiah
people.role: King of Judah in David’s royal line
people.relations: Son of Josiah and Hamutal. Uncle of Jehoiachin. Earlier name Mattaniah.
people.meaning: He is the third son of Josiah in the list. It tells no story about him. Verse 16 names another Zedekiah after Jeconiah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zedekiah, in Jeconiah’s line
people.role: Name in the descendants of Jehoiakim
people.relations: Listed after Jeconiah among the sons of Jehoiakim in 3:16.
people.meaning: Verse 16 lists him after Jeconiah, under the sons of Jehoiakim. The list tells no story about him. Verse 15 names a Zedekiah among Josiah’s sons.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.role: Descendant in the royal line after captivity
people.relations: Listed as Pedaiah’s son. Brother of Shimei.
people.meaning: The list names him as a son of Pedaiah. His children include Meshullam, Hananiah, and their sister Shelomith. Ezra calls him Shealtiel’s son.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shelomith, Zerubbabel’s daughter
people.role: Zerubbabel’s daughter in the royal list
people.relations: Daughter of Zerubbabel. Sister of Meshullam and Hananiah.
people.meaning: The list names her as the sister of Meshullam and Hananiah. It tells no story about her.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jabez
people.role: Man whose prayer breaks into the family list
people.relations: His mother names him. She says she bore him with sorrow.
people.meaning: He is more honorable than his brothers. He asks God to bless him and enlarge his border. He asks God to keep him from evil. God grants what he asks.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Bithiah
people.role: Pharaoh’s daughter in a Judah family record
people.relations: Daughter of an unnamed Pharaoh. Wife of Mered.
people.meaning: She is a daughter of Pharaoh, and Mered takes her as wife. Verse 18 speaks of her sons. It is not clear which names are hers.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Caleb
people.role: Son of Jephunneh who receives Hebron’s fields
people.relations: Son of Jephunneh. Father of Iru, Elah, and Naam.
people.meaning: His sons are Iru, Elah, and Naam. In chapter 6 he receives the fields and villages of Hebron. The sons of Aaron receive the city and its pasture lands. Chapter 2 names a Caleb who is Hezron’s son.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Simeon
people.role: Son of Israel whose tribe lives near Beersheba
people.relations: Son of Israel. Father of Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
people.meaning: His sons are Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul. His families live at Beersheba, Ziklag, and other towns until David’s reign. They do not grow like the children of Judah. Later some take pasture near Gedor, and five hundred go to Mount Seir.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Reuben
people.role: Firstborn whose family appears east of the Jordan
people.relations: Son of Jacob and Leah. Brother of Joseph.
people.meaning: He is Israel’s firstborn. He defiles his father’s couch, so his birthright goes to Joseph’s sons. His sons are Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. His families live east of Gilead until Assyria carries them away.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joseph
people.role: Ancestor whose sons receive the birthright
people.relations: Son of Jacob and Rachel. Husband of Asenath. Father of Ephraim and Manasseh.
people.meaning: He is a son of Israel. Reuben loses the birthright, and it goes to Joseph’s sons. The prince still comes from Judah.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Beerah
people.role: Reubenite leader carried away by Assyria
people.relations: Son of Baal in the line of Joel.
people.meaning: He is prince of the Reubenites. Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria carries him away captive.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pul / Tiglath Pileser
people.role: Assyrian king who takes the eastern tribes captive
people.relations: Verse 26 names both Pul and Tilgath Pilneser as king of Assyria.
people.meaning: Verse 6 says Tilgath Pilneser carries away Beerah, prince of the Reubenites. In verse 26 God stirs up Pul and Tilgath Pilneser. He carries away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. He brings them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jeroboam, son of Joash
people.role: Northern king used to date a family record
people.relations: Son of Israel’s Joash. Father of Zechariah. Usually called Jeroboam II.
people.meaning: Verse 17 names him as king of Israel beside Jotham king of Judah. The families of Gad were listed in their days. The chapter tells no story about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Levi
people.role: Ancestor of priestly and service families
people.relations: Son of Israel. Father of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
people.meaning: His sons are Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Chapter 6 traces priests, singers, and towns from these three. In chapter 23 David divides the Levites by the same three families.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Aaron
people.role: Priest whose sons serve at the altar
people.relations: Son of Amram and Jochebed. Father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
people.meaning: He is a son of Amram, and he has four sons. He and his sons offer on the altar and make atonement for Israel. He is set apart to burn incense and to bless in the LORD’s name. David divides his sons’ families for service by lot.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Moses
people.role: Servant of God whose commands guide worship
people.relations: Son of Amram and Jochebed. Brother of Aaron and Miriam. Husband of Zipporah.
people.meaning: He is a son of Amram and the brother of Aaron. The Levites carry the ark on poles, as Moses commanded. The tabernacle he made in the wilderness stands at Gibeon. David tells Solomon to keep the statutes the LORD gave Moses. His sons Gershom and Eliezer are counted with the tribe of Levi.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Miriam
people.role: Daughter of Amram and sister of Moses and Aaron
people.relations: Daughter of Amram. Sister of Aaron and Moses.
people.meaning: The list names her with Aaron and Moses as a child of Amram. It tells no story about her.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nadab
people.role: Son of Aaron named in the priestly family
people.relations: Son of Aaron. Brother of Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
people.meaning: He is the first of Aaron’s four sons in the list. He and Abihu die before their father and have no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar serve as priests.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abihu
people.role: Son of Aaron named in the priestly family
people.relations: Son of Aaron. Brother of Nadab, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
people.meaning: He is the second of Aaron’s four sons in the list. He and Nadab die before their father and have no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar serve as priests.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Eleazar
people.role: Aaron’s son whose family supplies sixteen priest groups
people.relations: Brother of Nadab, Abihu, and Ithamar.
people.meaning: He is Aaron’s third son and the father of Phinehas. Chapter 6 traces the priests from him down to Jehozadak. He serves as priest with Ithamar after Nadab and Abihu die. His family supplies sixteen of the twenty-four groups of priests.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ithamar
people.role: Aaron’s son whose family supplies eight priest groups
people.relations: Brother of Nadab, Abihu, and Eleazar.
people.meaning: He is Aaron’s fourth son. He serves as priest with Eleazar after Nadab and Abihu die. His family has eight heads of houses, and Eleazar’s has sixteen. Ahimelech is one of his sons’ line.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Phinehas
people.role: Priest who once ruled the gatekeepers
people.relations: Son of Eleazar. Grandson of Aaron.
people.meaning: He is the son of Eleazar and the father of Abishua. In time past he ruled over the keepers of the entry. Chapter 9 says the LORD was with him.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Samuel
people.role: Seer named in family lists and records
people.relations: Son of Hannah and Elkanah. Father of Joel and Abijah.
people.meaning: Chapter 6 names his sons Joel and Abijah. Heman the singer is his grandson. He and David set the gatekeepers in their office of trust. He dedicated gifts that Shelomoth keeps. A history of Samuel the seer records David’s acts.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Heman, the singer
people.role: Lead singer and the king’s seer
people.relations: Son of Joel, descendant of Samuel in chapter 6.
people.meaning: He is a Kohathite singer and the grandson of Samuel. The Levites choose him to sound bronze cymbals when the ark moves. He then serves at Gibeon with Jeduthun, with trumpets and cymbals. He is the king’s seer, and his fourteen sons serve in song.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Asaph, the singer
people.role: Chief of those who give thanks before the ark
people.relations: Son of Berechiah. Father of Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah.
people.meaning: He stands at Heman’s right hand. He sounds cymbals when the ark moves. David makes him chief of the Levites who give thanks before the ark. David leaves him there for each day’s work. His sons later serve under him with harps and cymbals.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ethan, the singer
people.role: Merarite musician beside Heman and Asaph
people.relations: Named with Kishi in chapter 6 and Kushaiah in chapter 15.
people.meaning: He is of the sons of Merari and stands at Heman’s left hand. The Levites choose him with Heman and Asaph. He sounds bronze cymbals when the ark moves.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehozadak
people.role: Priestly descendant taken into captivity
people.relations: Son of Seraiah in the priestly list.
people.meaning: He is the son of Seraiah, last in the list of priests. He goes into captivity when the LORD carries away Judah and Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar is the one who takes them.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ephraim
people.role: Ancestor who mourns his killed sons
people.relations: Son of Joseph and Asenath. Brother of Manasseh.
people.meaning: Men of Gath kill his sons Ezer and Elead in a fight over livestock. He mourns many days, and his brothers come to comfort him. His wife then bears a son, and he names him Beriah. The list then names Sheerah, who builds three towns.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Manasseh
people.role: Ancestor of northern and eastern family branches
people.relations: Son of Joseph and Asenath. Brother of Ephraim.
people.meaning: His concubine the Aramitess bears Asriel and Machir. Machir is the father of Gilead. The list also names Zelophehad, who has daughters.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zelophehad
people.role: Man whose daughters are noted in Manasseh’s list
people.relations: Named in Machir’s family. He has daughters.
people.meaning: The list names him in Machir’s family. It says only that he had daughters.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Sheerah
people.role: Woman who builds three towns
people.relations: Named as Ephraim’s daughter in this family sequence.
people.meaning: She builds Beth Horon the lower and the upper. She also builds Uzzen Sheerah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joshua
people.role: Son of Nun in Ephraim’s family list
people.relations: Son of Nun. He later leads Israel in the book of Joshua.
people.meaning: He is the son of Nun. His name ends a line that runs from Rephah through Elishama and Nun. The list tells no story about him.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Serah
people.role: Woman named in Asher’s family
people.relations: Sister of Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah.
people.meaning: She is the sister of Asher’s four sons. The list tells no story about her.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Benjamin
people.role: Ancestor of the family line leading to Saul
people.relations: Son of Rachel. Full brother of Joseph.
people.meaning: He is the father of Bela, Ashbel, Aharah, Nohah, and Rapha. The chapter names his families in Geba, Aijalon, Gibeon, and Jerusalem. It ends with Saul’s family.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Saul
people.role: First king whose death leads into David’s reign
people.relations: Son of Kish. Father of Jonathan, Merab, Michal, and other children.
people.meaning: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa and kill his sons. Archers overtake Saul, and he falls on his sword. The chapter says he died because he did not keep the LORD’s word. The LORD turns the kingdom over to David.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jonathan
people.role: Saul’s son who dies on Mount Gilboa
people.relations: Brother of Merab and Michal. Son of Saul.
people.meaning: The family list names him first among Saul’s sons. His son is Merib-baal. The Philistines kill him with his brothers Abinadab and Malchishua on Mount Gilboa. David’s nephew Jonathan in chapter 20 is another man.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Mephibosheth, Jonathan’s son
people.role: Merib-baal, Jonathan’s son in Saul’s family
people.relations: Son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul. Father of Micah.
people.meaning: The list calls him Merib-baal. He is Jonathan’s son and the father of Micah. Samuel calls him Mephibosheth. The list tells no story about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ishbosheth
people.role: Eshbaal, Saul’s son in the family list
people.relations: Son of Saul. Brother of Jonathan, Malchishua, and Abinadab.
people.meaning: The list calls him Eshbaal. He is the last of Saul’s four sons in the list. Samuel tells about his rule after Saul’s death.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shallum, the gatekeeper
people.role: Chief gatekeeper in Jerusalem
people.relations: Son of Kore, descendant of Ebiasaph and Korah.
people.meaning: He is chief of the gatekeepers. He and his Korahite brothers keep the thresholds of the tent. Their fathers kept the entry of the LORD’s camp. Verse 31 names Mattithiah as the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Mattithiah, the baker
people.role: Levite over things baked in pans
people.relations: Firstborn of Shallum the Korahite.
people.meaning: He is a Levite and the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite. He has the office of trust over the things baked in pans.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Saul’s armor bearer
people.role: Unnamed attendant who dies after Saul
people.relations: Companion of Saul in his final battle.
people.meaning: Saul asks him to draw his sword and kill him. He will not, for he is terrified. Saul falls on his own sword. When he sees that Saul is dead, he falls on his sword and dies.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jashobeam
people.role: Warrior and leader in David’s lists
people.relations: Called son of a Hachmonite in chapter 11 and son of Zabdiel in chapter 27.
people.meaning: He is chief of the thirty. He lifts his spear against three hundred and kills them at one time. He leads the army division for the first month. A Korahite named Jashobeam joins David at Ziklag, perhaps another man.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Eleazar
people.role: Son of Dodo who fights beside David
people.relations: Son of Dodo the Ahohite. One of the three mighty men.
people.meaning: He is with David at Pasdammim when the people flee from the Philistines. They stand in a plot of barley and defend it. They kill the Philistines, and the LORD saves them by a great victory.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Benaiah
people.role: Son of Jehoiada leading David’s guard and a division
people.relations: Son of Jehoiada. From Kabzeel.
people.meaning: He kills the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He kills a lion in a pit on a snowy day. He takes a tall Egyptian’s spear and kills him with it. David sets him over his guard, and he leads the third month’s division.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Uriah
people.role: Hittite warrior in David’s list
people.relations: Called a Hittite. Husband of Bathsheba.
people.meaning: The list of mighty men names Uriah the Hittite. It tells no story about him. Samuel tells how David ordered his death.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Amasai, the warrior
people.role: Chief of the thirty who pledges peace
people.relations: Chief of the thirty. He speaks for men of Benjamin and Judah.
people.meaning: Men of Benjamin and Judah come to David’s stronghold. David asks if they come to help or to betray him. The Spirit comes on Amasai, and he says, “We are yours, David.” David receives them and makes them captains.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zadok
people.role: Priest who serves under David and Solomon
people.relations: Son of Ahitub. Father of Ahimaaz.
people.meaning: A young warrior named Zadok comes to David at Hebron with twenty-two captains. David calls Zadok the priest and Abiathar to bring up the ark. Zadok then offers burnt offerings at Gibeon. He helps David divide the priests by lot. The assembly anoints him priest when Solomon is made king.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abinadab
people.role: Man whose house holds the ark
people.relations: The ark is in his house. Uzza and Ahio drive the cart from there.
people.meaning: The ark is in his house at Kiriath Jearim. David and all Israel bring it out on a new cart. The chapter tells nothing more about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Uzza / Uzzah
people.role: Ark attendant who dies during the first journey
people.relations: He drives the cart with Ahio from Abinadab’s house.
people.meaning: He and Ahio drive the cart that carries the ark. The oxen stumble at Chidon’s threshing floor. Uzza puts out his hand to hold the ark. The LORD strikes him, and he dies there. David is afraid and leaves the ark with Obed-Edom.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahio
people.role: Man who drives the ark cart with Uzza
people.relations: He drives the cart with Uzza from Abinadab’s house.
people.meaning: He and Uzza drive the new cart from Abinadab’s house. The chapter says nothing more about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Obed Edom
people.role: Gittite whose house keeps the ark
people.relations: Called the Gittite in chapter 13.
people.meaning: David carries the ark aside into his house. It stays three months, and the LORD blesses his house. David later brings the ark up from his house with joy. Chapter 15 also names an Obed-Edom among the doorkeepers and harp players.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hiram
people.role: King of Tyre who sends cedar and workers
people.relations: King of Tyre. He sends messengers to David.
people.meaning: He sends messengers to David with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters. They are to build David a house. David then sees that the LORD has made him king.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abiathar
people.role: Priest David calls to move the ark
people.relations: Priest named with Zadok. Father of Ahimelech in 24:6.
people.meaning: David calls Abiathar and Zadok to make ready and bring up the ark. Chapter 27 names him after Ahithophel, the king’s counselor.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Chenaniah, the musical leader
people.role: Chief Levite over the singing
people.relations: Chief of the Levites. He teaches the singers.
people.meaning: He is over the singing when the ark comes up. He teaches the singers because he is skillful. He wears fine linen with the singers and the Levites. Other translations word his task differently.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Michal
people.role: Saul’s daughter watching the ark celebration
people.relations: Daughter of Saul. Wife of David.
people.meaning: She looks out a window as the ark comes into David’s city. She sees King David dancing and playing. She despises him in her heart.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jeduthun
people.role: Musician who gives thanks with the harp
people.relations: Father of sons who serve in music and at the gate.
people.meaning: He serves at Gibeon with Heman, giving thanks with trumpets and cymbals. His sons are at the gate. Later his sons serve under him in the LORD’s house. He prophesies with the harp, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Obed Edom, son of Jeduthun
people.role: Gatekeeper identified as Jeduthun’s son
people.relations: Son of Jeduthun in 16:38.
people.meaning: David leaves him and Hosah as doorkeepers before the ark. The same verse names an Obed-Edom with sixty-eight relatives. The text does not say if they are one man.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hosah
people.role: Merarite gatekeeper and household head
people.relations: Father of Shimri, Hilkiah, Tebaliah, and Zechariah.
people.meaning: David leaves him as a doorkeeper before the ark. He is of the children of Merari. He makes Shimri chief, though Shimri is not the firstborn. The lot gives him and Shuppim the west gate.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nathan
people.role: Prophet who brings God’s answer to David
people.relations: Prophet who speaks with David. A history of David’s acts bears his name.
people.meaning: David tells him that the ark sits in a tent. Nathan says, “Do all that is in your heart.” That night God tells him that David shall not build the house. Nathan tells David that the LORD will build him a house.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hadadezer
people.role: King of Zobah whom David defeats
people.relations: King of Zobah. Syrians of Damascus come to help him. Shophach is his captain.
people.meaning: David defeats him toward Hamath and takes chariots, horsemen, and footmen. David takes his gold shields and much bronze from his cities. Later his captain Shophach leads Syrians against David and dies. His servants then make peace with David and serve him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Tou / Toi
people.role: Tou, king of Hamath who greets David
people.relations: Father of Hadoram. Hadadezer had wars with him.
people.meaning: He hears that David has struck Hadadezer’s army. Hadadezer had wars with Tou. He sends his son Hadoram to greet and bless David. Hadoram brings vessels of gold, silver, and bronze.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hadoram / Joram, son of Tou
people.role: Hadoram, Tou’s son sent to David
people.relations: Son of Tou king of Hamath.
people.meaning: His father Tou sends him to greet and bless King David. He brings vessels of gold, silver, and bronze. David dedicates them to the LORD.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahimelech, son of Abiathar
people.role: Priest who helps divide the priests
people.relations: Son of Abiathar in 24:6. Called Abimelech in the reading of 18:16.
people.meaning: Verse 18:16 calls him Abimelech and lists him as priest with Zadok. He is of the sons of Ithamar. He helps David and Zadok divide the priests for service. He is present when Shemaiah writes the lots.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shavsha
people.role: Scribe among David’s officials
people.relations: Named with Joab, Zadok, and Benaiah.
people.meaning: The list of David’s officials names him as scribe. It tells no story about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hanun
people.role: Ammonite king who shames David’s messengers
people.relations: Son and successor of Nahash.
people.meaning: His father Nahash dies, and David sends men to comfort him. His princes say the men came to spy. Hanun shaves them, cuts their garments, and sends them away. He then hires chariots and horsemen, and war follows.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nahash
people.role: Ammonite king who was kind to David
people.relations: King of the children of Ammon. Father of Hanun.
people.meaning: He dies, and his son reigns in his place. David says that Nahash showed him kindness. So David sends men to comfort Hanun.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shophach
people.role: Captain of Hadadezer’s army
people.relations: Captain of the army of Hadadezer.
people.meaning: He leads the Syrians who come from beyond the River. David crosses the Jordan and fights them. The Syrians flee, and David kills Shophach.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Sibbecai
people.role: Warrior who kills Sippai and leads a division
people.relations: Called a Hushathite.
people.meaning: The list of mighty men names Sibbecai the Hushathite. In the war at Gezer he kills Sippai, of the sons of the giant. The Philistines are subdued. He leads the army division for the eighth month. Samuel gives a different name for the man he kills.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Elhanan, son of Jair
people.role: Warrior who kills Lahmi
people.relations: Son of Jair in this chapter.
people.meaning: He kills Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite. Samuel’s parallel verse uses different names. Chapter 11 names an Elhanan who is the son of Dodo.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Lahmi
people.role: Philistine warrior killed by Elhanan
people.relations: Called the brother of Goliath.
people.meaning: He is the brother of Goliath the Gittite. Elhanan kills him in a war with the Philistines. Samuel’s parallel verse has different wording.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jonathan, David’s nephew
people.role: David’s nephew who kills a giant at Gath
people.relations: Son of Shimea, David’s brother, in 20:7.
people.meaning: A man of great stature at Gath has twenty-four fingers and toes. He defies Israel. Jonathan kills him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Goliath
people.role: Philistine named as Lahmi’s brother
people.relations: Called the Gittite. Brother of Lahmi.
people.meaning: The chapter names him only as Lahmi’s brother. It calls him Goliath the Gittite. In this verse Elhanan kills Lahmi.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Gad
people.role: David’s seer who brings a choice and a command
people.relations: David’s seer. He carries the LORD’s words to David.
people.meaning: The LORD tells him to offer David three things. Gad names them: famine, enemies, or pestilence. Later the angel tells Gad to send David to Ornan’s threshing floor. David goes and builds an altar there. A history of Gad the seer records David’s acts.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ornan / Araunah
people.role: Ornan, Jebusite owner of the threshing floor
people.relations: A Jebusite. Father of four sons. He deals with David.
people.meaning: He is threshing wheat when he sees the angel. David asks to buy the threshing floor. Ornan offers it free, with oxen, wood, and wheat. David pays six hundred shekels of gold and builds an altar.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ornan’s four sons
people.role: Four unnamed sons who hide from the angel
people.relations: Four sons with Ornan at the threshing floor.
people.meaning: They are with Ornan while he threshes wheat. Ornan sees the angel, and they hide.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Gershom, Moses’ son
people.role: Ancestor in the service families
people.relations: Son of Moses. Father of Shebuel.
people.meaning: He is a son of Moses. His son Shebuel is chief and rules over the treasuries. The list tells no story about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Eliezer, Moses’ son
people.role: Ancestor in the service families
people.relations: Son of Moses. Father of Rehabiah.
people.meaning: He is a son of Moses. He has one son, Rehabiah, whose sons are very many. Shelomoth, who keeps the dedicated things, comes from him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shemaiah, the scribe
people.role: Levite who writes down the priests’ lots
people.relations: Son of Nethanel.
people.meaning: He is a Levite, the son of Nethanel. He writes down the lots for the priests. He does so before the king, the princes, Zadok, and Ahimelech.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Obed Edom, the gatekeeper
people.role: Head of a family that keeps a gate and storehouse
people.relations: Father of eight sons named in chapter 26.
people.meaning: He has eight sons, “for God blessed him.” Sixty-two of his family are able men for the service. The lot gives him the south gate and his sons the storehouse. The text does not say if he is the Gittite of chapter 13.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Meshelemiah
people.role: Head of a family of gatekeepers
people.relations: Son of Kore. Father of Zechariah and six other named sons.
people.meaning: He is a Korahite, the son of Kore. He has seven sons, and Zechariah is the firstborn. The east gate falls by lot to Shelemiah, another form of his name. Zechariah, a wise counselor, receives the north gate.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shelomoth, the treasurer
people.role: Keeper of the dedicated things
people.relations: From the family of Eliezer, the son of Moses.
people.meaning: He and his brothers are over the treasuries of the dedicated things. David and the captains dedicated plunder to repair the LORD’s house. Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab also dedicated gifts. All of it is under his hand.

people.name: Shebuel, the treasurer
people.role: Ruler over the treasuries
people.relations: Son of Gershom, the son of Moses.
people.meaning: He is the son of Gershom, the son of Moses. He is chief among Gershom’s sons. He is ruler over the treasuries.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abner
people.role: Son of Ner who dedicated gifts
people.relations: Son of Ner. Named beside Saul among those who dedicated gifts.
people.meaning: He dedicated gifts, and Shelomoth keeps them. The chapter tells nothing more about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahithophel
people.role: The king’s counselor
people.relations: The king’s counselor. Jehoiada and Abiathar come after him.

people.name: Hushai
people.role: The king’s friend
people.relations: Called the Archite. Named beside Ahithophel.
people.meaning: The list calls Hushai the Archite the king’s friend. It tells no story about him.

people.name: Obil
people.role: Ishmaelite over the king’s camels
people.relations: Called the Ishmaelite.

people.name: Jaziz
people.role: Hagrite over the king’s flocks
people.relations: Called the Hagrite.
people.meaning: He is over King David’s flocks. The list tells no story about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehiel, the Gershonite
people.role: Gershonite who keeps the precious stones
