places.name: Adullam · broad locality
places.summary: In chapter 11, three of the thirty chief men go down to David. He is at the cave of Adullam. The Philistines camp in the valley of Rephaim.
places.limits: The marker shows the general area. The cave’s exact place is not certain.

places.name: Aram · broad region
places.summary: The children of Ammon hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-maacah and nearby lands (chapter 19). Joab and David defeat the Syrians. The Syrians then make peace with David.
places.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.

places.name: Assyria · broad northern Mesopotamian region
places.summary: The king of Assyria carries away Beerah, prince of the Reubenites (chapter 5). He also carries away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
places.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: Judah is carried away captive to Babylon for disobedience (chapter 9). Chapter 3 calls Jeconiah “the captive.”
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Simeon’s families live at Beersheba until David’s reign (chapter 4). David tells Joab to count Israel from Beersheba to Dan (chapter 21).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Beth Horon · upper and lower town region
places.summary: Beth Horon is given to Kohath’s families (chapter 6). Sheerah builds Beth Horon the lower and the upper (chapter 7).
places.limits: One marker stands for two towns, the lower and the upper.

places.name: Bethel · proposed locality
places.summary: Bethel and its towns belong to the children of Joseph (chapter 7).
places.limits: The site is a proposal. The marker shows the general area.

places.name: Bethlehem
places.summary: Chapter 2 calls Salma the father of Bethlehem. In chapter 11 a Philistine garrison holds the town. Three mighty men break through and draw water from its well for David. David pours it out to the LORD.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Damascus
places.summary: Syrians of Damascus come to help Hadadezer (chapter 18). David strikes twenty-two thousand of them. He puts garrisons there, and they bring tribute.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Dan · broad northern locality
places.summary: David tells Joab to count Israel from Beersheba to Dan (chapter 21). Dan marks one end of the count.
places.limits: The marker shows the general area in the north.

places.name: Edom · broad region
places.summary: Chapter 1 lists kings who reigned in Edom before Israel had a king. In chapter 18 Abishai strikes eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. Garrisons are put in Edom, and all the Edomites serve David.
places.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.

places.name: Gath · Tell es-Safi
places.summary: Men of Gath kill Ephraim’s sons Ezer and Elead (chapter 7). Men of Aijalon put Gath’s people to flight (chapter 8). David takes Gath and its towns from the Philistines (chapter 18). Jonathan kills a giant there (chapter 20).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Gezer
places.summary: Gezer is given to Kohath’s families (chapter 6). It lies at the west of Joseph’s lands (chapter 7). David strikes the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer (chapter 14). Sibbecai kills Sippai in a war there (chapter 20).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Gibeon
places.summary: Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lives there with his family (chapters 8 and 9). David strikes the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer (chapter 14). The LORD’s tabernacle and altar stand at the high place there (chapters 16 and 21). Zadok offers burnt offerings there morning and evening.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Mount Gilboa · broad setting
places.summary: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa (chapter 10). Saul and his three sons die there.
places.limits: The marker shows the mountain’s general location.

places.name: Gilead · broad region
places.summary: Reuben’s livestock grow in Gilead, and Gad’s families live there (chapter 5). Ramoth in Gilead goes to Merari’s families (chapter 6). In David’s fortieth year, mighty men are found at Jazer of Gilead (chapter 26).
places.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.

places.name: Hamath
places.summary: David defeats Hadadezer toward Hamath (chapter 18). Tou king of Hamath sends his son Hadoram with gifts for David.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Hebron
places.summary: Six sons are born to David in Hebron (chapter 3). The city goes to Aaron’s sons, and its fields to Caleb (chapter 6). All Israel anoints David king there (chapter 11). Armed men from the tribes come and feast three days (chapter 12).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Jabesh Gilead · broad locality
places.summary: The men of Jabesh Gilead hear what the Philistines did to Saul (chapter 10). They take the bodies of Saul and his sons. They bury the bones under the oak in Jabesh and fast seven days.
places.limits: The marker shows the general area. The exact site is not certain.

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Hanun shames David’s messengers (chapter 19). David tells them to stay at Jericho until their beards grow.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: David takes the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites (chapter 11). He brings the ark into a tent there (chapters 15 and 16). He buys Ornan’s threshing floor and builds an altar (chapter 21). He gathers the leaders there and gives Solomon the temple plans (chapter 28).
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Jordan · crossing area uncertain
places.summary: Gadites cross the Jordan in flood to join David (chapter 12). David crosses it with all Israel to fight the Syrians (chapter 19).
places.limits: The text does not say where they crossed. The marker shows the river in general.

places.name: Kiriath Jearim
places.summary: Chapter 2 calls Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim. In chapter 13 David and all Israel go there for the ark. They bring it out of Abinadab’s house on a new cart. The chapter also calls the town Baalah.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Moab · broad region
places.summary: David defeats Moab (chapter 18). The Moabites become his servants and bring tribute. David dedicates silver and gold from Moab to the LORD.
places.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.

places.name: Rabbah · Amman
places.summary: Joab besieges Rabbah while David stays at Jerusalem (chapter 20). Joab strikes the city and overthrows it. David takes the king’s crown and much plunder.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Valley of Rephaim · broad setting
places.summary: The Philistines camp in the valley of Rephaim (chapter 11). David is in the stronghold then. They raid the valley twice (chapter 14). David asks God each time and defeats them.
places.limits: The valley’s exact place is not certain. The marker shows the general area.

places.name: Shechem
places.summary: Shechem, a city of refuge, is given to Kohath’s families (chapter 6). Shechem and its towns belong to the children of Joseph (chapter 7).
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Sidon
places.summary: The Sidonians and the people of Tyre bring cedar trees to David (chapter 22). He gathers the wood for the LORD’s house.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Tyre
places.summary: Hiram king of Tyre sends cedar, masons, and carpenters to build David’s house (chapter 14). People of Tyre later bring cedar for the temple (chapter 22).
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Ziklag · uncertain locality
places.summary: Simeon’s families live at Ziklag until David’s reign (chapter 4). David stays there while he hides from Saul (chapter 12). Men of Benjamin and Manasseh join him there.
places.limits: The site of Ziklag is not certain. The marker shows a general area.

steps.title: Names place a small community in a larger past
steps.text: Verse 1 is three names with no verb. The list assumes readers know the stories from Genesis. It starts with all humanity before it narrows. Verses 5–23 name many nations, and only then comes Abraham (verse 27). Verse 34 uses the name Israel, not Jacob. Edom, Israel’s neighbor and rival, receives twenty verses (verses 35–54). The book sets one people’s history inside the history of everyone.

steps.title: A failed procession changes the next one
steps.text: Verse 13 is David’s answer to the question he asked in 13:12. He says “we,” and so includes himself in the fault. The fault was not carrying the ark as the rule required. Verses 2 and 15 state the correction: Levites, poles, and shoulders. Exodus 25:14 and Numbers 4:15 gave those instructions. The joy of the first attempt remains in the second. Now it is ordered, with named singers and leaders (verses 16–22).

steps.title: Royal giving rests on a prior gift
steps.text: Verses 2–8 list gifts on a huge scale. In verse 14 David refuses to take credit for them. Everything comes from God, and the givers return what was his. Verse 15 calls Israel strangers and temporary residents, as their fathers were. The king says this while holding land, city, and throne. Verse 9 traces the people’s joy to giving willingly. Verse 17 says God tests the heart and is pleased with honesty.
